title: Introduce atomic GPU upgrade plan, state-bridge and snapshotter TF modules
author: Aisha Patel
description: This PR adds two new terraform modules (state-bridge and state-snapshotter) and an orchestration pattern for performing atomic, zero-downtime upgrades of GPU node pools in Private deployments. Motivation: customers running heterogeneous GPU profiles and tenant-scoped nodepools need a migration path that avoids global tfstate drift, prevents orphaned subnets, and allows safe, testable rollbacks. What this PR delivers: 1) modules/state-bridge: lightweight, opt-in bridge resource that mirrors minimal nodepool and subnet ownership metadata across tfstate boundaries to support phased cutovers; 2) modules/state-snapshotter: ordered snapshot artifacts (S3-compatible) that capture a snapshot of relevant resources (nodepool tags, lease indexes, iam bindings) in a plan-friendly format to enable deterministic rollbacks; 3) modules/gpu_pool: upgrade lifecycle hooks and a plan-only lifecycle mode that gates destructive changes behind an explicit 'apply-phase' variable; 4) modules/iam: ephemeral upgrade role templates and rotation-friendly policies to be assumed only during upgrade windows; 5) network-claim-scheduler: terraform helper and accompanying controller helm values to pin subnets for the duration of a rolling upgrade to avoid cross-tenant eviction; 6) example upgrade CLI (scripts/upgrade-plan.sh) and a migration doc (examples/private/upgrade-zero-downtime.md) that show canary -> staggered cutover -> finalize sequence. Migration notes and backwards compatibility: modules are opt-in and default to no-op; existing tfstate users can adopt the state-bridge by supplying a bridge backend config to preserve owner references; snapshotter stores artifacts under the same backend bucket with an upgrade-run UUID and is configurable for retention. Rollback story: apply of the plan-only mode will never destroy nodepools until 'apply-phase' is toggled; the snapshotter supports a deterministic rollback script that restores the minimal state and reclaims leases. Testing and verification: included integration test harness (tests/upgrade_plan_integration_test.go) that exercises a simulated two-tenant upgrade and verifies no tenant-level downtime; CI runs a local acceptance suite and policy checks. Checklist: run ./scripts/upgrade-plan.sh --preview; run integration tests; coordinate with infra SRE for IAM window; verify snapshots are uploaded and can be listed; manually review IAM ephemeral role bindings. Related: references ENG-4812 and infra runbook INF-2101 for on-call procedures.

release_notes: Add opt-in terraform modules to enable atomic/zero-downtime GPU nodepool upgrades in private deployments. Provides state-bridge and snapshotter modules, new IAM ephemeral roles for upgrade windows, plan-only lifecycle mode, and example upgrade scripts. Backwards compatible and opt-in.
